spans.s:
1. अ-दिति, इस्, f., Ved. having nothing to give, desti-
tution; for 2. अदिति, 3. अ-दिति, see below.

अदिति 2. अदिति, इस्, m. (fr. rt. अद्), Ved.
devourer, i. e. death; for 1. अ-दिति, see above.

अदिति 3. अ-दिति, इस्, इस्, इ (rt. 4. दा or दो,
द्यति; for 1. अ-दिति, see above), not tied, free; bound-
less; unbroken, entire, unimpaired; happy; pious; (इस्),
f. freedom, security, safety; boundlessness, immensity;
inexhaustible abundance; unimpaired condition, per-
fection; creative power; अदिति, the mother of the
Ādityas, or of the gods; a cow; a wife; milk; the
earth; speech (as symbols of the above ideas).
—अदिती,
du., Ved. heaven and earth.
—अदिति-ज or अदिति-
नन्दन, अस्, m. a son of Aditi, an Āditya, a divine
being.
—अदिति-त्व, अम्, n. the condition of Aditi, or
of freedom, unbrokenness, &c.

3. अ-दिति; add — Aditi was daughter of Dakṣa
and wife of Kaśyapa.

अदिक्क अ-दिक्क, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. having no
share in the horizon, banished from beneath the sky.

आदिक, अस्, आ, अम्, (used like आदि, q. v., at the end
of compounds) beginning with, et cætera, and so on.

अदित्सत् अ-दित्सत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, or अ-दित्सु,
उस्, उस्, उ (Desid. fr. rt. दा), not inclined to give.

अदिप्रभृति अदि-प्रभृति, इस्, m., अद् &c., i. e.
belonging to the second class of roots [cf. अद्-आदि].

अदीक्षित अ-दीक्षित, अस्, आ, अम्, one who
has not performed the consecrating ceremony (दीक्षा)
connected with the Soma sacrifice; one who is not
concerned in that ceremony; one who has not re-
ceived Brāhmanical consecration.

अदीन अ-दीन, अस्, आ, अम्, not depressed;
not low; noble-minded; rich happy; (अस्), m., N. of
a prince, also called Ahīna.
—अदीन-सत्त्व, अस्, आ,
अम्, possessing undepressed (or unimpaired) goodness
or mettle.
—अदीनात्मन् (˚न-आत्˚), आ, आ, अ, unde-
pressed in spirit; high-spirited.

अदीपित अ-दीपित, अस्, आ, अम्, not illumin-
ated.
आ-दीपित, अस्, आ, अम्, illuminated, inflamed.

अदीर्घ अ-दीर्घ, अस्, आ, अम्, not long.
—अदीर्घ-सूत्र, अस्, आ, अम्, not dilatory, not
tedious, prompt.

आदि आदि, इस्, m. (fr. 1. आ-दा ?), beginning,
commencement; a firstling, first-fruits; first, prior,
prime, pre-eminent; (very often at the end or in the
middle of a compound in the sense) beginning with,
et cætera, and so on (e. g. इन्द्रादयः सुराः, the
gods beginning with Indra, i. e. Indra &c.; गृहादि-
युक्त, possessed of houses, &c.; एवम्-आदीनि वस्-
[]
तूनि, such and similar things; शय्या खट्वादिः,
the word शय्या means a bed &c.); आदौ, ind. in the
commencement or beginning, at first; [with this
word has been compared the Slav. jedin, ‘one.’]
—आदि-कर, अस्, m. the creator; an epithet of
Brahmā.
—आदि-कर्तृ, ता, m. the creator; an epi-
thet of Brahmā, Kṛṣṇa or Viṣṇu.
—आदि-कर्मन्,
अ, n. (in gram.) the beginning or commencement of
an action (as in the example सूर्यः प्रद्योतितः,
‘the sun has begun to shine;’ see
Gram. 895

. a).
—आदि-कवि, इस्, m. the first poet; an epithet of
Brahmā, or of Vālmīki.
—आदि-काण्ड, अम्, n. first
part or chapter; title of the first book of the Rāmā-
yaṇa.
—आदि-कारण, अम्, n. a primary cause; ana-
lysis, algebra.
—आदि-काल, अस्, m. primitive time,
remote antiquity.
—आदि-काव्य, अम्, n. the first poem,
an epithet of the Rāmāyaṇa.
—आदि-क्रित्, त्, m. the
creator; see आदि-कर्तृ above.
—आदि-केशव, अस्,
m. the first keśava, an epithet of Viṣṇu.
—आदि-तस्,
ind. from the beginning, from the first, in the be-
ginning, at first, at the head of (with gen.).
—आदि-
ता, f. or आदि-त्व, अम्, n. priority, precedence.
—आदि-देव, अस्, m. the first god, the creator; N. of
Brahmā, Viṣṇu or Kṛṣṇa, or Nārāyaṇa; the sun.
—आदि-दैत्य, अस्, m. epithet of Hiraṇyakaśipu.
—आदि-नाथ, अस्, m., N. of Ādi-buddha; N. of an
author.
—आदि-पर्वन्, अ, n. first section or chapter,
title of the first book of the Mahā-bhārata.
—आदि-
पुराण, अम्, n. the primitive Purāṇa, N. of the
Brahma-Purāṇa.
—आदि-पुरुष or आदि-पूरुष,
अस्, m. the first male or progenitor, usually applied to
Viṣṇu; the primeval spirit.
—आदि-बल, अम्, n.
generative power (first vigour).
—आदि-बुद्ध, अस्,
आ, अम्, perceived in the beginning; (अस्), m. the
primitive Buddha, the chief deity of the northern
Buddhists.
—आदि-भव, अस्, आ, अम्, produced at first;
(अस्), m. epithet of Brahmā.
—आदि-भूत, अस्, आ, अम्,
first-born or existent; (अस्), m., a N. of Brahmā.
—आदि-मत्, आन्, अती, अत्, having a beginning
—आदि-
मूल, अम्, n. primitive foundation, primeval cause.
—आदि-योगाचार्य (˚ग-आच्˚), अस्, m. primitive
teacher of devotion; an epithet of Śiva.
—आदि-
रस, अस्, m. the first or chief of the eight rasas, the
principal sentiment or emotion, i. e. sṛṅgāra or love.
—आदिरस-श्लोक, अस्, m., N. of a poem supposed to
be written by Kālidāsa.
—आदि-राज, अस्, m. the first
king; an epithet of Manu; of a son of Kuru; of
Pṛthu.
—आदि-वंश, अस्, m. primeval race, primitive
family.
—आदि-वराह, अस्, m. the first boar; N. of
Viṣṇu, alluding to his incarnation in that form.
—आदिवाराह, अस्, ई, अम्, relating to the first boar.
—आदि-विपुला, f., N. of a metre.
—आदि-शरीर, अम्,
n. the primitive body.
—आदि-सर्ग, अस्, m. primitive
creation.
—आदि-सूर, अस्, m., N. of a prince.
—आदी-
श्वर (˚दि-ईश्˚), अस्, m., N. of a prince.
—आद्य्-अन्त,
अस्, आ, अम्, having beginning and end; from the be-
ginning to the end; (अम्), n. beginning and end,
first and last.
—आद्यन्त-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, having
beginning and end, finite.
—आद्य्-अन्तान्तर-वर्तिन्,
ई, इनी, इ, containing beginning, end, and middle;
being all in all.
—आद्य्-उदात्त, अस्, आ, अम्, having
the acute accent on the first syllable.
—आद्युदात्-
त-त्व, अम्, n. the condition of having the acute
accent on the first syllable.
—आद्योपान्तम् (˚द्य-
उप्˚), ind. from first to last.
आदिम, अस्, आ, अम्, first, prior, primitive, original.

आदिग्ध आ-दिग्ध, अस्, आ, अम् (rt. दिह्), be-
smeared.

आदितेय आदितेय, अस्, m. (fr. अदिति), a son
of Aditi; a god, a deity, a divinity.

आदित्य, अस्, आ, अम्, belonging or devoted to, or
originating from Aditi; belonging or relating to, or
originating from the Ādityas; (अस्), m. a son of
Aditi. In the earliest times this is the N. of seven
deities of the heavenly sphere, of whom Varuṇa is
the chief and to whom therefore especially belongs
the title Āditya. The names of six of the seven are
Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman, Bhaga, Dakṣa, and Aṃśa; that
of the seventh is not clearly ascertained. Sometimes their
number is supposed to be eight; and in the period of
the Brāhmaṇas twelve, as representing the sun in
the twelve months of the year. The name Āditya
was afterwards applied to any god, though especially
applicable to Sūrya, the sun; N. of Viṣṇu in his
Vāmana or dwarf avatār, as son of Kaśyapa and Aditi
and younger brother of Indra; the plant Calotropis
Gigantea; N. of a man; (औ), m. du., N. of a constel-
lation, the seventh lunar mansion.
—आदित्य-केतु, उस्,
m., N. of a son of Dhṛta-rāṣṭra.
—आदित्य-गर्भ,
अस्, m., N. of a Bodhi-sattva.
—आदित्य-चन्द्रौ,
m. du. sun and moon.
—आदित्य-दास, अस्, m., N. of
a man.
—आदित्य-पत्त्र, अस्, m. a plant = अर्क-
पत्त्र.
—आदित्य-पर्णिनी, f. a creeping plant with
gold-coloured flowers, growing near the banks of
water.
—आदित्य-पुराण, अम्, n., N. of an Upa-
purāṇa.
—आदित्य-पुष्पिका, f. red swallow wort.
—आदित्य-प्रभ, अस्, m., N. of a king.
—आदित्य-
भक्ता, f. = अर्क-भक्ता, q. v.
—आदित्य-मण्डल,
अम्, n. the disc or orb of the sun.
—आदित्य-वत्, आन्,
अती, अत्, surrounded by the Ādityas.
—आदित्य-वनि,
इस्, इस्, इ, Ved. winning the (favour of the) Ādityas.
—आदित्य-वर्ण, अस्, आ, अम्, having the colour of
the sun; (अस्), m., N. of a man.
—आदित्य-वर्मन्,
आ, m., N. of a king.
—आदित्य-व्रत, अम्, n. = अर्क-
व्रत, q. v.
—आदित्य-सदृश, अस्, ई, अम्, like the
sun.
—आदित्य-सूनु, उस्, m., son of the sun; N. of
Sugrīva, the monkey-king; of Yama, Saturn, Sāvarṇi
Manu, and Vaivasvata Manu.
—आदित्य-सेन, अस्, m.,
N. of a king of Ujjayinī.
—आदित्याचार्य (˚त्य-आच्),
अस्, m., N. of an author.

आदित्सा आ-दित्सा, f. (fr. Desid. of 1. आ-दा),
desire to seize or take.

आ-दित्सु, उस्, उस्, उ, wishing to take or have (with
acc.).

आदिन् आदिन्, ई, इनी, इ (rt. अद्), eating (used
at the end of compounds; cf. अन्नादिन् &c.).

आदिनव आदिनव, अम्, n. (?), Ved. misfor-
tune, hinderance, want of luck (in dice); see आदीनव.
—आदिनव-दर्श, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. having evil
designs towards a fellow-player at dice.

आदीनव आदीनव, अस्, m. distress, pain, un-
easiness; fault, transgression; an afflicter of distress.

आदिश् 1. आ-दिश्, cl. 6. P. A. -दीशति, -ते,
-देष्टुम्, to aim at, to assign; to point out, indicate,
report, announce, teach, determine, specify, foretel;
to order, direct, command; to provoke, challenge; to
undertake, try; to profess as one's purpose or duty:
Caus. -देशयति, -यितुम्, to indicate, announce.

2. आ-दिश्, क्, f., Ved. aiming at, design, intention;
project, proposition; proposal, declaration; region,
quarter; (Sāy.) a sacrifice offered or assigned (to a
particular deity).
आ-दिश्य, ind. announcing, apprising, aiming at.

आ-दिष्ट, अस्, आ, अम्, advised, enjoined; directed,
commanded; said; (अम्), n. command, order; frag-
ments or leavings of a meal.

आदिष्टिन्, ई, इनी, इ, or (ई), m. one who receives
instruction, a pupil, a student, a Brāhman in the first
order or quarter of his life; a penitent, one engaged
in any expiatory rite.

आदीप् आ-दीप्, Caus. P. -दीपयति, -यितुम्,
to cause to blaze, kindle, set on fire, illuminate.

आ-दीपन, अम्, n. setting on fire, inflaming, ex-
citing, embellishing; whitening the wall, floor or
seat &c. upon festival occasions.
आ-दीप्त, अस्, आ, अम्, set on fire, blazing up.
आ-दीर्य, ind. having split, showing fissures.

आ-दीपक, अस्, m. one who sets fire to anything,
an incendiary.
